Record Class CompositeMapping

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.CompositeMapping
Record Components:
name - mapping name, unique within a Mappings instance
keySystem - formal identifier of the key code system, may be null
valueSystem - formal identifier of the value code system, may be null
parts - the names of the mappings asked, in order; never empty
override - whether this declaration is meant to replace a mapping of the same name loaded earlier
All Implemented Interfaces:
Mapping
public record CompositeMapping(String name, String keySystem, String valueSystem, List<String> parts, boolean override) extends Record implements Mapping
A mapping that holds no entries of its own but the names of other mappings - its parts - and answers through them. It exists for sources that spread one translation over several tables, the common case being a FHIR ConceptMap whose groups translate one source code system into several target systems. Each group is a SimpleMapping; the composite over them lets a caller ask the ConceptMap as a whole without knowing which groups it has or which one holds a code.

A lookup asks the parts in declaration order, in two rounds:

  1. the first part that declares an entry for the key answers;
  2. only if no part does, the first part whose fallback answers.
So a code declared in the second part is found even if the first part has a fallback that would answer anything - which is how FHIR's $translate reads all groups of a ConceptMap when no target system is given. Reverse lookups work the same way.

Since the parts may translate into different code systems, a plain lookup cannot say which system an answer belongs to; Mappings.translate(String, String) returns it along with the code, taken from the part that answered. The composite's own keySystem() and valueSystem() are whatever its creator declares; the ConceptMap loader sets those that its parts share, and null where they differ.

The parts must be simple mappings registered before the composite, so composites do not nest. No file format declares one - loaders create them - and no MappingWriter writes one: its parts are written instead.

Since:
6.0

      public final boolean equals(Object o)
      Indicates whether some other object is "equal to" this one. The objects are equal if the other object is of the same class and if all the record components are equal.
